components.basis: Durrett p.1 (sigma-field as a nonempty collection closed under complements and countable unions; countable = finite or countably infinite; reason for omitting intersections; measurable space), p.3 (generated sigma-field), p.4 (algebra or field): definition present; the nonempty and field variants are stated and proved equivalent on the route.
Durrett p.1 (countable intersections) and p.3 (intersection of an arbitrary nonempty family of sigma-fields; smallest sigma-field): every clause proved in the annex.

Durrett Example 1.1.6 p.4 (finite/cofinite subsets of the integers form an algebra that is not a sigma-algebra): the example is worked on the positive integers and the source form on the integers is recorded with its locator.
Durrett pp.1-2 (measure as nonnegative countably additive set function with empty value zero; probability measure; probability space triple): definition and the nonnegative-sum convention present.

Durrett Theorem 1.1.1 p.2 (monotonicity, subadditivity in covering form, continuity from below, continuity from above under mu(A_1)<infinity) with its proof: all four items proved; the covering form of subadditivity is stated, proved and related to the union form.

Durrett Example 1.1.2 p.2 (discrete probability spaces; the most general probability measure on such a space) and the astragali p.3: grouping, construction and converse proved; astragalus model given with its four weights.
Handbook worked example (no separate source item): total mass, tail events, empty decreasing intersection and parity probabilities all computed.

Boundary for the finiteness premise of Durrett Theorem 1.1.1(iv) p.2: counting-measure failure, no uniform mass on the positive integers, and the finitely additive finite/cofinite assignment without countably additive extension, each argued.
Durrett p.3 (Borel sets of R^d as smallest sigma-field containing the open sets; R and R^d notation): definition and the notation dictionary present.
Durrett Examples 1.3.2-1.3.3 p.15 (closed real rays, open rational rays, open rectangles with real endpoints, open sets) and Exercises 1.1.2-1.1.3 p.9: every generator class proved.

Durrett sec.1.2 p.10 (random variable, X in F notation, any function on a discrete space) and sec.1.3 p.15 (measurable map, random vector for d>1, reason for arbitrary targets): all present with the membership notation bridged.
Durrett Theorem 1.3.1 and (1.3.1) p.15, Exercise 1.3.1 p.17: generator test, sigma(X) as smallest sigma-algebra and its generation proved.
Handbook worked example: sigma(Y) listed and non-measurability of X for sigma(Y) shown.

Durrett p.10 (indicator; characteristic-function terminology) and Exercise 1.3.7 pp.17-18 (simple functions as finite combinations of indicators): definitions present and the two descriptions proved equivalent.
Durrett Theorems 1.3.4-1.3.6 pp.15-16 (composition; Borel functions of several random variables; sums) and the cX, X^2, sin X remark: all proved, Theorem 1.3.5 in its Borel-function form.

Durrett pp.16-17 (Omega_o, almost sure convergence without a named limit, almost everywhere, X_infinity = limsup, R* with its order topology, random variables on an event D): definition present; every source form stated and bridged with proofs.
Durrett Theorem 1.3.7 p.16 and measurability of the convergence set: inf, sup, liminf, limsup, finite limits, convergence event and simple approximation proved.
Durrett p.10 (distribution mu(A)=P(X in A), Figure 1.3 P o X^{-1}), pp.11-12 (equal in distribution, X =d Y), Example 1.2.8 p.13 (point mass as a law): all forms present.
Durrett p.10 (check that the distribution is a probability measure): proved with the image-law, atomic and countable-target formulas.
Durrett app. A.1 p.456 (pi-system, lambda-system (i)-(iii), the rectangle example, attribution to Dynkin): definitions match the source; example and attribution recorded and proved.

Durrett Theorems A.1.4-A.1.5 pp.456-458 (pi-lambda theorem; uniqueness for measures on F_1, F_2 agreeing on a pi-system with an exhausting finite-measure sequence): both proved; the finiteness condition shown necessary by example.
Durrett p.10 (distribution function F(x)=P(X<=x)) and the left-limit notation of Theorem 1.2.1(iv) p.11: present.

Durrett Theorem 1.2.1 (i)-(v) p.11 with proof, equal in distribution iff equal distribution functions pp.11-12 (via Theorem 1.1.4), Exercise 1.2.3 p.14: every item proved, including the Stieltjes-uniqueness route.
Durrett p.13 (discrete distribution; Example 1.2.8) and Example 1.2.9 p.14 (dense discontinuities): jump reading worked; discrete laws and the dense-jump example stated and proved.

Boundary locators checked: thm.1.2.2 p.11 (Lebesgue measure on (0,1)), thms.1.1.4 p.3 and 1.1.9 p.5 with app. A.1 (existence), secs.1.4-1.6 pp.18-36 (integrals, Fatou 1.5.5, dominated convergence 1.5.8, expected value). The deferred existence results are proved in the following chapter.
Durrett p.53 (R^N, coordinates, product sigma-field from finite-dimensional sets) and app. A.3 pp.464-465 (rectangles with infinite endpoints allowed; semialgebra and its algebra): present.
Durrett Theorem 2.1.21 p.53 / A.3.1 p.464 consistency condition: stated in the source form; sufficiency of bounded rectangles proved.
Durrett A.3 pp.464-465 (semialgebra; finite additivity through finitely many coordinates): every clause proved.
Durrett A.3 p.465 (compact closed rectangles in the approximation): definitions present; tightness proved.
Durrett Lemma A.3.3 p.465 (sets C_n of closed rectangles inside B_n with small defect, unproved in the source): proved, including compactness of closed rectangles.
Durrett Lemma A.3.3 pp.465-466 (B_n decreasing to the empty set forces P(B_n) to 0; compact approximation and diagonal argument): proved with explicit dimensions replacing the repeating-sets device.
Durrett Theorem 2.1.21 p.53 = Theorem A.3.1 p.464 with proof via Theorem A.1.1 pp.464-465: existence and uniqueness proved.
Durrett p.53 (finite independent construction and its infinite extension) and Example A.3.2 p.464: proved.
Durrett p.53 (nice spaces; standard Borel name declined) and Exercise 2.1.3 p.55: conventions present; the source definition of nice is stated and its exact relation to Borel real codings proved.
Durrett Theorem 2.1.22 proof p.54 (expansion with infinitely many zeros; interleaving .x^1_1 x^1_2 x^2_1 x^1_3 x^2_2 x^3_1 ...): theta(j,k) reproduces the source order.
Durrett p.54 (special case [0,1)^N with the weighted metric and phi_o): image, inverse and measurability proved.
Durrett Theorem 2.1.22 p.54 (d = rho/(1+rho), dense sequence, psi, composite map; caveat emptor): construction completed and proved; the source statement in its own terms and the caveat recorded.

Durrett p.53 (failure for arbitrary spaces with the Andersen-Jessen, Halmos p.214, Neveu p.84 and Wegner attributions; trivial generalization to nice spaces): coded extension proved; attributions recorded; nice-space form settled with proof.
Handbook worked boundary: inconsistent marginals and a null infinite intersection, both argued.
Durrett p.54 (cardinality of Borel sets via Dudley sec.13.1): the boundary records that a separate argument is needed; the statement and its proof are supplied on the route.
Kernel framing of Durrett's mu: Omega x S -> [0,1] p.214: definition present.

Durrett p.214 definition (i) version for each A, (ii) probability measure for a.e. omega; regular conditional probability when S=Omega: the every-argument form and the source almost-everywhere form both present.
Durrett Theorem 4.1.16 p.214 with its indicator-simple-monotone-signed proof: proved for kernels and for the source almost-everywhere definition.
Durrett Theorem 4.1.17 proof p.215 (rational versions, F(x,omega)=inf over q>x, lambda-system argument): every CDF condition, measurability, conditional identity and uniqueness written.

Durrett Theorem 4.1.17 p.215 (nice S; image step) and the nonexistence remark p.214 (Dieudonne 1948, Doob 1953 p.624, Faden 1985; accumulating exceptional sets): Borel-coding form proved; the nice-space form settled with a failure example; nonexistence claim and attributions recorded.
Durrett continuation of Example 4.1.6 p.214 (joint density f>0): proved for f>=0 with explicit exceptional observation set, which contains the source case.
Durrett Theorem 4.1.18 p.215 (X, Y in a nice space, kernel on observation values): proved with an arbitrary conditioning space; the source form on nice spaces settled.
Supports Durrett p.214 remark that regular conditional distributions compute all conditional expectations at once: joint measure, iterated integral and conditional version proved.
Durrett Exercise 4.1.4 p.216 (conditional Hoelder via regular conditional probability; integrability implicit in the definition of conditional expectation p.205): proved.
Durrett Example 4.1.8 p.210 (Borel's paradox; customary and great-circle coordinate ranges): both coordinate systems specified; the source framing and name recorded.

Durrett Example 4.1.8 p.210 (theta uniform, angle not; independence makes the conditional law the unconditional one; more surface near the equator): densities, independence and the conditional law proved; the second null-event example computed.
Boundary: existence restricted to the standard Borel target class, consistent with the source remark p.214 that regular conditional distributions need not exist.

defect_observations.note: Equality of the product and trace sigma-algebras on E^(n) asserted through common generators; the trace side rests on thm:p15-measurability-criterion applied to the inclusion, not cited.

Classes shown to contain the whole space and to be closed under complements and countable disjoint unions are called lambda-systems; def:p15-pi-lambda (measurable-probability.tex 400-408) uses proper differences and increasing unions. The bridge (B minus A = complement of the disjoint union of A and B^c; increasing unions as disjoint unions of successive differences) is routine but unwritten. Same pattern at lines 211-217 and 279-288. Not counted as missing coverage.

Generation of the target sigma-algebra by phi-preimages of rational half-lines is asserted; it follows from phi being a measurable isomorphism and the generator statement of thm:p15-measurability-criterion, which is not cited. Same at lines 232-233.
Null probability of coordinate boundary overlaps asserted; immediate from the density.
